text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended firmer after breaking nearby $320 resistance. August ended up $2.50 at $321.40 per tonne, while October closed $2.90 higher at $311.50 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York settled higher and over resistance, setting the market up for further gains on Thursday, trade sources said. It was added that July is poised to challenge the key 11.20 cents/lb based on today's close above 11.11 cents/lb. July added 10 points to close at 11.15 cents/lb, while October closed 8 points higher at 10.92 cents/lb. But solid producer selling around current levels could prove too great a hurdle to overcome, they added.

In any case there does not seem to be any fundamental reason for a pronounced rise in world market prices. Traders are still watching whether US trade house Cargill will find buyers for Brazilian and Central American raw sugar delivered against May futures in New York, adding that it was trying to sell the sugar to Russian refiners. Recently, talk that Cargill would find buyers for more than 300,000 tonnes of Brazilian and Central American raw sugar underpinned positive sentiment in New York. Russia meets most of its needs by importing whites from Ukraine and refining Cuban raws and its own sugar beets.

UNITED STATES - Total sugar imports under the 1996/97 (October/September) tariff rate quota up to May 11, 1997 amounted to 968,907 tonnes, raw value, which is equivalent to 46 per cent of the total tariff rate quota of 2.100 million tonnes. The largest countries of origin up to May 11 were the Dominican Republic with 149,861 tonnes, Brazil with 115,023 tonnes and the Philippines with 100,600 tonnes.

DENMARK - The weather in the week ended May 18 continued to be changeable with temperatures ranging somewhat above average. Precipitation levels since April 1 were between 51 and 102 mm compared to the long term mean of 61 to 65 mm. Growth is reported to be very good. Many farmers have sprayed herbicides for the second time but conditions are difficult. Some regions report pest attacks. The overall crop outlook is normal.

CUBA - Cuban sugar exports continued at their sluggish pace in March with the overall total for that month reaching no more than 786,167 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 1.011 million tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 1.874 million tonnes, down from 2.166 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Major countries of destination in October/March 1996/97 were Russia with 534,402 tonnes, raws, sharply down from 1.235 million tonnes, Egypt with 276,523 tonnes against 40,402 tonnes and China with 212,073 tonnes, up from 142,020 tonnes, figures supplied by the International Sugar Organization show.

The European Union awarded 37,500 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 43.069 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on May 21. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to May 21 reached 2,033,600 tonnes, which compares to 2,158,198 tonnes last year.
